sentences.text: Heard Mr. R. Ali, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Also heard Mr. K.K. Das,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State/respondent No.1 and Ms. D. Saikia, learned Amicus Curiae for the respondent No. 2.
2.

By this application filed under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraskha Sanhita, 2023, the accused petitioner namely, Jamir Ali @ Jomir, has prayed for bail in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 110/2024 (corresponding to Barbari P.S. case no. 33/2024) under Section 366/376(3) of IPC r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been detained in custody since 05.08.2024.
It is also submitted that the allegation leveled against the is totally false and concocted.
After completion of investigation, the investigating officer submitted charge sheet vide C.S. No. 30/2024 dated 25.9.2024.

It is further submitted that out of 9(nine) witnesses, 3(three)
witnesses have already been examined including the victim.
The victim girl (PW3) has made a contradictory statement before the trial court and which does not inspire any confidence for conviction of the accused/petitioner.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner has also pointed out that in the case of Gobindaraju vs.
State of Karnataka, reported in 2021 (3) Crl.L.J. 98, wherein it was held that "conviction without providing opportunity to the accused to cross examine the prosecution witness is nothing but denial of a fair Page No.# 3/5 trial."

sentences.text: Considering the background of the case as well as length of the detention, the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.

5. On the other hand, Mr. Das, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has submitted that the victim is a minor girl and she has implicated the petitioner in her evidence before the trial court that due to such physical relationship, the victim became pregnant.
Hence, he has opposed in granting bail to the petitioner.

6. Ms. Saikia, learned Amicus Curiae for the respondent No.2 has also submitted that the petitioner had committed such nuisance to the victim girl for which she became pregnant and gave birth to a child.
As such, she has strongly opposed in granting bail to the petitioner.
7. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
I have also perused the trial court record.
8. It appears from the evidence of the victim girl that the petitioner had committed sexual intercourse with the victim for which she became pregnant and gave birth to a child.
Admittedly, the victim is a minor girl as per documents available in the record.

sentences.text: 14. Ordinarily in serious offences like rape, murder, dacoity, etc., once the trial commences and the prosecution starts examining its witnesses, the Court be it the Trial Court or the High Court should be loath in Page No.# 4/5 entertaining the bail application of the accused.

15. Over a period of time, we have noticed two things, i.e., (i) either bail is granted after the charge is framed and just before the victim is to be examined by the prosecution before the trial court, or (ii) bail is granted once the recording of the oral evidence of the victim is complete by looking into some discrepancies here or there in the deposition and thereby testing the credibility of the victim.
16.
We are of the view that the aforesaid is not a correct practice that the Courts below should adopt.
Once the trial commences, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion which may either result in the conviction of the accused or acquittal of the accused.

The moment the High Court exercises its discretion in favour of the accused and orders release of the accused on bail by looking into the deposition of the victim, it will have its own impact on the pending trial when it comes to appreciating the oral evidence of the victim.

It is only in the event if the trial gets unduly delayed and that too for no fault on the part of the accused, the Court may be justified in ordering his release on bail on the ground that right of the accused to have a speedy trial has been infringed...."

10. In view of the aforesaid legal proposition as well as considering the materials available in the trial court record, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the petitioner at this stage of trial.
Therefore, prayer for the bail is rejected.
Page No.# 5/5 11.
The bail application stands disposed of accordingly.
